body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

In multi-agent ADK workflows, every invoke_model activity shows the same generic summary in the Temporal UI timeline. TemporalModel already has access to adk_agent_name via llm_request.config.labels["adk_agent_name"], but doesn't use it in the default summary. This makes it hard to follow what's happening when multiple agents are running.

### Describe the solution you'd like

The default activity summary for invoke_model could include the agent name when it's available in labels — e.g. invoke_model: Fleet Agent instead of just invoke_model. This would make multi-agent workflows significantly easier to trace in the UI without requiring any user-side customization.

### Additional context

This feedback is based on the Python SDK's ADK integration, but the same pattern applies to other SDK implementations of TemporalModel. We worked around this by subclassing TemporalModel and pulling the agent name from labels.

This pattern was identified while working on the ADK/Temporal NEXT demo: https://github.com/temporal-community/ice-cream-fleet-demo

Tracking: AI-62 (https://temporalio.atlassian.net/browse/AI-62)

comments.body:
The agent name in activity summary is a straightforward quality-of-life improvement that also has security implications — in multi-agent Temporal workflows, "invoke_model" repeated 50 times gives no indication of which agent is responsible for which actions, making post-incident attribution very difficult.

From a behavioral trust perspective, named activities are also the first requirement for meaningful per-agent behavioral monitoring. If you cannot distinguish `invoke_model: FleetAgent` from `invoke_model: PricingAgent` in the timeline, you cannot track per-agent error rates, latency patterns, or cost distributions — which are the raw inputs for behavioral trust scoring.

The `labels["adk_agent_name"]` path you identified is the right anchor. A few additional label keys worth including in the default summary if present:

```python
def _default_summary(self, llm_request):
    agent_name = llm_request.config.labels.get("adk_agent_name", "")
    agent_id = llm_request.config.labels.get("agent_id", "")       # unique identity
    trust_tier = llm_request.config.labels.get("trust_tier", "")   # T0-T4 if set

    parts = ["invoke_model"]
    if agent_name:
        parts.append(agent_name)
    if trust_tier:
        parts.append(f"[{trust_tier}]")
    return ": ".join(parts)  # e.g. "invoke_model: FleetAgent [T2]"
```

The trust tier in the summary is optional but useful for operators scanning the timeline — immediately visible whether a high-privilege (T3/T4) agent was involved in an incident without having to open individual activity details.

title: [Feature Request]  Include agent name in default TemporalModel activity summary
